=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: Line 3516 (the `}${support_checkout_changes}"` continuation line)
  Problem: YAML block-scalar syntax error. The shell assignment `remaining_changes="${remaining_changes:+${remaining_changes}` on line 3515 embeds a literal newline, causing the closing `}` to land at column 1 on line 3516.
  Why it fails at runtime: YAML block scalars (introduced by `run: |`) require content lines to be indented. A bare `}` at column 1 terminates the block scalar early and is then parsed as a YAML flow-mapping end marker, producing `expected <block end>, but found '}'`.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 3514-3516 (the multi-line variable assignment)
  Problem: The `}` of the `${remaining_changes:+${existing}...}` expansion lands at indentation column 0 because of the literal newline embedded in the shell string.
  Why it fails at runtime: Adjacent lines in the block scalar have 16-18 spaces of indentation. The fix must avoid a bare `}` at column 1 — the simplest bash-compatible approach is `$'\n'`: `remaining_changes="${remaining_changes:+${remaining_changes}$'\n'}${support_checkout_changes}"`.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 3511-3512 (`git -C "${support_checkout}" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | sed "..." || true`)
  Problem: The `|| true` swallows all non-zero exits from the inner `git status --porcelain` pipeline, so a transient filesystem error, a corrupted `.git` directory, or any unexpected failure mode produces an empty `support_checkout_changes` — identical to "no changes."
  Why it fails at runtime: Real inner-checkout modifications would be silently dropped from `remaining_changes`.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- Requirement: "Validation — implement.yml parses as valid YAML; the added multi-line construct passes bash -n" (PR Description / Validation section)
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/implement.yml line 3516
  Evidence of absence: The file does NOT parse as valid YAML. `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` raises `ConstructorError` at line 3516 column 1. The CI lint job (`yamllint`) also fails. The PR's own validation claim is false.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: 3514-3516 (the continuation of the multiline `remaining_changes=...` assignment)
  Problem: The line `}${support_checkout_changes}"` (starting with `}`) appears inside a double-quoted YAML scalar that is later parsed as a heredoc-like block for GitHub Actions `GITHUB_OUTPUT` and shell.
  Why it fails at runtime: This triggers a `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'` inside yamllint's `rules/indentation.py:343` (expected indent becomes None). The lint job (`yamllint ... .github/workflows/*.yml`) aborts with exit 1 before any workflow step can run; the `codex-agent` job stays incomplete and the PR cannot merge.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: 3509 (the inner `git -C "${support_checkout}" status --porcelain ... || true`) and 3515-3516 (concatenation into `remaining_changes`)
  Problem: Failures from the inner checkout query (`git -C` on a missing/corrupt nested repo, permission error, etc.) are swallowed by `|| true`; the subsequent `if [ -n "${support_checkout_changes}" ]` never sees output and the splice never happens. The concat `remaining_changes="${remaining_changes:+${remaining_changes} }${support_checkout_changes}"` can also produce a leading newline or malformed line when `remaining_changes` is empty.
  Why it fails at runtime: A dirty inner checkout that should trigger Guard 1 is silently dropped from `remaining_changes`, so the no-op path is taken instead of escalation → `ai:needs-human`. The outer `grep -vxE` on consumer runs already strips top-level `??` markers; this compounds the loss of signal.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

LAST RUN DIFF and PR DIFF contain none of these corrections.
